11.title: Catch a Bad Number: handle ValueError
11.description: Implement `parse_lives(text)` to return the integer value when possible and `None` when int conversion raises ValueError. Do not catch unrelated exceptions.
11.learningObjective: Catch the specific ValueError raised when user text cannot be converted to an integer.
instructions: Call int(text) inside a try block.
Catch ValueError only.
Return the integer after successful conversion.
Return None for invalid numeric text.

workedExample.explanation: Narrow exception handling makes expected invalid input recoverable without hiding programming errors such as a misspelled variable.

11.hint: int raises ValueError when a string is not a valid integer representation.
11.explanation: Narrow exception handling makes expected invalid input recoverable without hiding programming errors such as a misspelled variable.

12.title: Separate the Success Path: use try and else
12.description: Implement `read_count(text)` to convert text to an integer. Return `("invalid", None)` on ValueError and `("valid", count)` only in the try/else success path.
12.learningObjective: Use an else clause for work that should run only when a try block completes without an exception.
instructions: Keep only the conversion in the try block.
Catch ValueError and return the invalid result.
Use else for the successful count result.
Do not place the conversion itself in else.

workedExample.explanation: Keeping the try block small makes it clear which operation is expected to fail. The else clause separates normal processing from recovery.

13.title: Clean Up Every Time: use finally
13.description: Implement `parse_with_status(text, state)` to set `state["busy"]` true, attempt integer conversion, return the integer or None for ValueError, and always set busy to false in finally.
13.learningObjective: Place unconditional cleanup in a finally clause so it runs after success and after a handled failure.
instructions: Set busy to true before conversion.
Convert the text inside try.
Catch ValueError and return None.
Reset busy to false in finally.

workedExample.explanation: A finally block is suited to cleanup that must happen on every path. For real files and locks, a context manager is often clearer when available.

13.hint: finally runs even when the function returns from the try or except clause.

14.title: Reject an Invalid Score: raise ValueError
14.description: Implement `validate_score(score)` to return valid scores unchanged and raise ValueError with the message `score must be between 0 and 100` for values below 0 or above 100.
14.learningObjective: Raise a clear ValueError when a score falls outside the inclusive 0–100 range.
instructions: Check whether score is less than 0 or greater than 100.
Raise ValueError with the requested message when invalid.
Return the original score when it is valid.

15.title: Missing Lesson: define a domain exception
15.description: Define `LessonNotFoundError` as a subclass of LookupError. Implement `get_lesson(catalog, slug)` to return a matching lesson or raise LessonNotFoundError with the missing slug in its message.
15.learningObjective: Create and raise a domain-specific exception when a requested lesson does not exist.
instructions: Define LessonNotFoundError as a LookupError subclass.
Check whether slug is present in catalog.
Return the associated lesson when it exists.
Raise the custom exception with the missing slug otherwise.

workedExample.explanation: A domain-specific exception communicates the reason for failure while remaining compatible with code that catches LookupError.

15.hint: A custom exception can specialize an established built-in category so callers can catch the failure precisely.
